stem:
Esha looks at the figure. Segments $AB$ and $CD$ meet at $M$, and a square mark sits at $\angle AMC$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $\angle AMC$ is a right angle, so $AB$ and $CD$ are perpendicular at $M$.
$AB$ and $CD$ are perpendicular at $M$ for any crossing of the two segments, even without a right angle at $M$.
Every pair of segments drawn through $M$ must form a straight angle at $M$.
The answer is "right angle" only because the square mark is the darkest print near $M$.

teacher.key_rationale: A square mark names a right angle, so AB and CD meet perpendicularly at M. Claiming perpendicularity for any crossing omits the right-angle condition. Forcing every meeting to be a straight angle over-scopes. Reading only the darkest print is surface capture.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source right triangle as crossing segments AB and CD with a square mark at angle AMC.
